  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.6,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R75"],
      "pins": ["R75.1", "R75.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R75 is annotated with value \"24k\", but its MPN and description identify a 24 Ω part (\"FRC0805J240TSD\", \"125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±5% 24Ω 0805\"). Its value field is three orders of magnitude off from the part it is built from.",
      "expected": "The value field should match the 24 Ω part actually specified (or the part should be changed to a 24 kΩ device to match the value).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R75\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R75 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24 Ω part is fitted, the resistor across the VOUTN/VOUTP rail is about 1000× lower than the schematic intends, loading that rail heavily and dissipating far more power than the 0805 part is rated for. If the 24 kΩ value is intended, the BOM part is wrong.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "short_to_ground",
      "components": ["U5"],
      "pins": ["U5.2", "U5.3"],
      "nets": ["GND", "Net-(U17-A)"],
      "observed": "Pin 2 (input A) of the SN74LVC1G07 buffer U5 sits on the GND net together with its pin 3 (GND). Its output Y (pin 4) drives Net-(U17-A), so the buffer can only ever drive that net low.",
      "expected": "The input A of a buffer in this signal chain should carry a logic signal, not ground. The other buffers in the design (U7, U14, U22, U26) have their inputs on real signal nets.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U5\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U5\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") (pintype \"output\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"206\") (name \"Net-(U17-A)\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "The buffer input is stuck at logic low, so the signal it should pass to U17 is lost. The indicator or control function fed through U17 cannot respond to its intended source.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D3", "D45", "D12"],
      "pins": ["D3.2", "D45.2", "D12.2"],
      "nets": ["NET0170"],
      "observed": "The anodes of D3, D45 and D12 form net NET0170, and that net contains no other pins. No supply rail or driver reaches it, so the LED anode net is floating. Their cathodes are driven through R60, R9 and R31 from the CM4's Ethernet nLED and activity pins.",
      "expected": "The common LED anode net should be tied to the 3.3 V rail, as the other indicator LEDs in the design are (for example D15 and D35 are tied to +3V3 or driven through resistors from it).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"41\") (name \"NET0170\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D3\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D45\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D12\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The three Ethernet/activity LEDs cannot conduct, so they never light. The status indication for link and activity is lost. Board function is unaffected, but the diagnostic feature is broken.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows a mismatched resistor value on R75 (24k annotated, 24 Ω part specified), a buffer input (U5.2) tied to ground, and an isolated LED anode net (NET0170) with no supply connection. The value and open-connection findings are the most clearly supported by the files; the U5 ground tie is a plausible deviation from the intended signal chain."
}

anomalies.observed: R75 is annotated with value "24k", but its MPN and description identify a 24 Ω part ("FRC0805J240TSD", "125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±5% 24Ω 0805"). Its value field is three orders of magnitude off from the part it is built from.
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the 24 Ω part actually specified (or the part should be changed to a 24 kΩ device to match the value).
anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is fitted, the resistor across the VOUTN/VOUTP rail is about 1000× lower than the schematic intends, loading that rail heavily and dissipating far more power than the 0805 part is rated for. If the 24 kΩ value is intended, the BOM part is wrong.

anomalies.observed: Pin 2 (input A) of the SN74LVC1G07 buffer U5 sits on the GND net together with its pin 3 (GND). Its output Y (pin 4) drives Net-(U17-A), so the buffer can only ever drive that net low.
anomalies.expected: The input A of a buffer in this signal chain should carry a logic signal, not ground. The other buffers in the design (U7, U14, U22, U26) have their inputs on real signal nets.
anomalies.impact: The buffer input is stuck at logic low, so the signal it should pass to U17 is lost. The indicator or control function fed through U17 cannot respond to its intended source.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of D3, D45 and D12 form net NET0170, and that net contains no other pins. No supply rail or driver reaches it, so the LED anode net is floating. Their cathodes are driven through R60, R9 and R31 from the CM4's Ethernet nLED and activity pins.
anomalies.expected: The common LED anode net should be tied to the 3.3 V rail, as the other indicator LEDs in the design are (for example D15 and D35 are tied to +3V3 or driven through resistors from it).
anomalies.impact: The three Ethernet/activity LEDs cannot conduct, so they never light. The status indication for link and activity is lost. Board function is unaffected, but the diagnostic feature is broken.
